The measles outbreak in West Texas started in a Mennonite community with a 48% vaccine exemption rate—not immigrants. But let’s be clear: Open borders under Biden’s administration did create systemic risks. The Chicago migrant shelter outbreak in 2024 proved low vaccination rates among arrivals, per CDC data. 

H.R. 746, the America First Act, tackles this head-on by blocking federal benefits for unvaccinated non-citizens, protecting public health. Blaming immigrants for Texas’ outbreak is wrong, but dismissing the broader threat of unchecked migration is reckless. 

Both low domestic vaccination and porous borders endanger Americans. Fixing one without the other is half-measure theater.

Recognizing local efforts to assist seniors with Medicare coverage is commendable, but let’s not ignore the systemic rot in federal healthcare bureaucracy. While Hitcho Insurance provides free consultations to navigate this maze, Medicare itself remains a fiscal disaster—fraudulent billing costs taxpayers $60B annually, and administrative bloat consumes 8% of spending compared to 2% in private insurance.

The real issue? Washington’s refusal to streamline Medicare’s 1,200+ pages of regulations that force agencies like Hitcho to clean up the mess. Redirecting even 10% of Medicare’s $900B budget from paperwork to patient care would do more for seniors than any broker’s Band-Aid.

Efficiency starts with gutting bureaucracy, not applauding those forced to navigate it.

The Nancy Gardner Sewell Medicare Multi-Cancer Early Detection Screening Coverage Act (S. 339) claims to expand cancer screening but reeks of bureaucratic overreach. Section 2(a) forces Medicare to cover unproven blood tests starting in 2028, locking payment rates to existing stool DNA tests ($641+ per test) without cost controls.

With 70% of cancers already detected in Medicare patients, this risks billions in redundant screenings while Section 2(b)(2) bizarrely restricts testing to those under 68+ (increasing yearly).

Prioritizing speculative tech over proven diagnostics? Classic DC: fund Pharma’s pet projects while underfunding mammograms/colonoscopies that save lives today.
